title: From Ram Rauni’s Battle to the Valour of Kaura Mal

blocks.text: The page first closes the Ram Rauni struggle by looking back on the battle and on the fate awaiting Shah Nawaz after his earlier arrogance. It acts as a retrospective seal on the siege narrative before the story shifts to the next political and military movement.

The new emphasis falls on Episode 121 and on Kaura Mal as a devout Sikh ally whose sympathies lie with the Panth rather than with persecutors. The text presents Kaura Mal as a devout Sikh ally who supports prayer, congregation, and practical assistance rather than empty courtly display.

This creates a marked tonal change from siege endurance to alliance and initiative. The Khalsa is no longer merely surviving a cordon; it is preparing to move with support from a figure whose piety and courage are central to the next episode.
